## pyMSAviz · Install + Theory {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · setup]{.eyebrow}

### Five lines for a Clustal-style alignment figure

```bash
pip install pyMSAviz
```

```{.python}
from pymsaviz import MsaViz       # the one class that does everything
```

**Theory.** `pyMSAviz` reads **FASTA / Clustal / PHYLIP / Stockholm** alignment
files (or a Biopython `MultipleSeqAlignment`), applies a **standard colour
scheme** (`Clustal`, `Zappo`, `Taylor`, `Nucleotide`, …), draws a **consensus
track** at the bottom, prints **per-column letter counts**, and **wraps** long
alignments across multiple rows. The output is a matplotlib `Figure`, so
the cream-canvas rcParams and IBM Plex Mono apply automatically. Day-2 `_03`
taught the primitives; this is the same picture, in five lines.


<!-- slide 26 -->
## pyMSAviz · The Data {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · data peek]{.eyebrow}

### Synthesise 8 DNA sequences × 80 cols, write FASTA

`MsaViz` expects a file path or a biopython object. We build a small toy
alignment in numpy (same approach as day-2 `_03`), then dump it to a temporary
FASTA file. Print the first few sequences as a sanity check.

```{python}
#| echo: true
from pathlib import Path                                        # for temp file path
import tempfile                                                 # cross-platform temp dir

# build a small DNA alignment: 8 seqs x 80 cols, ~5% mutation, one indel
n_rows, n_cols = 8, 80                                          # alignment shape
bases  = np.array(list("ACGT"))                                 # alphabet
base   = rng.choice(bases, size=n_cols)                         # ancestor sequence
aln    = np.tile(base, (n_rows, 1))                             # 8 copies of ancestor
mutate = rng.random((n_rows, n_cols)) < 0.05                    # 5% substitution mask
mutate[0] = False                                               # keep seq0 as ancestor
aln[mutate] = rng.choice(bases, size=mutate.sum())              # apply substitutions
aln[5, 30:36] = "-"                                             # 6-col deletion in seq5

# write to a temp FASTA file so MsaViz can read it
fasta_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "toy_msa.fasta"      # OS-temp FASTA path
with open(fasta_path, "w") as fh:                               # plain FASTA writer
    for i, row in enumerate(aln):                               # one record per row
        fh.write(f">seq{i}\n" + "".join(row) + "\n")            # header + sequence

print("wrote:", fasta_path)                                     # confirm file location
print("first 2 sequences:")
for i in range(2):                                              # print 2 records
    print(f">seq{i}", "".join(aln[i, :60]), "...")              # header + first 60 bases
```


<!-- slide 27 -->
## pyMSAviz · Step 1 — Simplest Viz {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · build]{.eyebrow}

### 1 · `MsaViz(fasta).plotfig()` returns a matplotlib Figure

`MsaViz(path)` parses the alignment, picks a default colour scheme, and lays out
the figure. `.plotfig()` returns the **matplotlib `Figure`** — the cream-canvas
rcParams set in the theme apply automatically. Two lines.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="1|3-4|6-9"}
from pymsaviz import MsaViz                             # the one class

# fasta_path was written in the previous slide
mv = MsaViz(str(fasta_path))                            # CREATE — parse + lay out

# CALL — render to a matplotlib Figure (cream rcParams apply)
fig = mv.plotfig()                                      # returns plt.Figure
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 3.0)                           # fit our two-column width
plt.show()                                              # render in the slide
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from pymsaviz import MsaViz

n_rows, n_cols = 8, 80
bases  = np.array(list("ACGT"))
base   = rng.choice(bases, size=n_cols)
aln    = np.tile(base, (n_rows, 1))
mutate = rng.random((n_rows, n_cols)) < 0.05
mutate[0] = False
aln[mutate] = rng.choice(bases, size=mutate.sum())
aln[5, 30:36] = "-"
fasta_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "toy_msa.fasta"
with open(fasta_path, "w") as fh:
    for i, row in enumerate(aln):
        fh.write(f">seq{i}\n" + "".join(row) + "\n")

mv = MsaViz(str(fasta_path))
fig = mv.plotfig()
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 3.0)
plt.show()
```

## pyMSAviz · Step 2 — Colour Scheme {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · build]{.eyebrow}

### 2 · `color_scheme="Nucleotide"` for DNA

The default scheme is Clustal (protein-tuned). For DNA, switch to
`color_scheme="Nucleotide"` — A/C/G/T get distinct hues and gaps stay neutral.
For protein alignments use `"Clustal"`, `"Zappo"`, or `"Taylor"`. The scheme
choice is the single most visible knob in the whole library.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="3-6"}
from pymsaviz import MsaViz                             # the one class

# only one new keyword vs step 1 — explicit colour scheme for DNA
mv = MsaViz(
    str(fasta_path),                                    # the same toy alignment
    color_scheme="Nucleotide",                          # A/C/G/T-specific colours
)

fig = mv.plotfig()                                      # CALL — render Figure
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 3.0)                           # match our column width
plt.show()
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from pymsaviz import MsaViz

fasta_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "toy_msa.fasta"
# fasta written in the previous slide; reuse the file
mv = MsaViz(str(fasta_path), color_scheme="Nucleotide")
fig = mv.plotfig()
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 3.0)
plt.show()
```
:::

<!-- slide 29 -->
## pyMSAviz · Step 3 — Consensus + Counts + Wrap {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · build]{.eyebrow}

### 3 · The canonical Clustal viewer look

Three keyword arguments turn the bare grid into the full Clustal-viewer layout:
`show_consensus=True` adds the consensus row, `show_count=True` shows per-column
letter counts on the right axis, and `wrap_length=40` breaks the alignment
across multiple rows so 80 columns become two 40-wide stripes.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="3-9"}
from pymsaviz import MsaViz                             # the one class

# add three knobs: wrap, consensus row, per-column counts
mv = MsaViz(
    str(fasta_path),                                    # same toy alignment
    color_scheme="Nucleotide",                          # DNA colours
    wrap_length=40,                                     # wrap every 40 cols
    show_consensus=True,                                # bottom consensus row
    show_count=True,                                    # column number ticks
)

fig = mv.plotfig()                                      # CALL — render Figure
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 4.2)                           # taller — wrapped layout
plt.show()
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from pymsaviz import MsaViz

fasta_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "toy_msa.fasta"
mv = MsaViz(
    str(fasta_path),
    color_scheme="Nucleotide",
    wrap_length=40,
    show_consensus=True,
    show_count=True,
)
fig = mv.plotfig()
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 4.2)
plt.show()
```
:::

<!-- slide 30 -->
## pyMSAviz · Step 4 — Highlight a Region {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · build]{.eyebrow}

### 4 · `set_highlight_pos([(start, end)])` to spotlight a motif

`set_highlight_pos` takes a list of `(start_col, end_col)` tuples (1-indexed,
inclusive) and draws a box around each region. Use it to mark a motif, an
indel block, a primer site, anything you want the reader to look at first. We
spotlight the deletion block at columns 31–36.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```{.python code-line-numbers="3-9|11-13"}
from pymsaviz import MsaViz                             # the one class

# rebuild with the same wrapped, consensus look from step 3
mv = MsaViz(
    str(fasta_path),                                    # same alignment file
    color_scheme="Nucleotide",                          # DNA colours
    wrap_length=40,                                     # two rows of 40 cols
    show_consensus=True,                                # bottom consensus
    show_count=True,                                    # column counts axis
)

# box the indel region — columns 31..36 (1-indexed, inclusive)
mv.set_highlight_pos([(31, 36)])                        # one or many (start,end) pairs

fig = mv.plotfig()                                      # CALL — render Figure
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 4.2)                           # match step 3 height
plt.show()
```
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
from pymsaviz import MsaViz

fasta_path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "toy_msa.fasta"
mv = MsaViz(
    str(fasta_path),
    color_scheme="Nucleotide",
    wrap_length=40,
    show_consensus=True,
    show_count=True,
)
mv.set_highlight_pos([(31, 36)])
fig = mv.plotfig()
fig.set_size_inches(9.5, 4.2)
plt.show()
```
:::
::::


<!-- slide 31 -->
## pyMSAviz · Takeaway {.smaller}

[pyMSAviz · recap]{.eyebrow}

### When an MSA needs to look like an MSA viewer

::: {.takeaway}
[The recipe]{.tl}
1. **`MsaViz(fasta)`** parses any FASTA / Clustal / PHYLIP / Stockholm file.
2. **`color_scheme=`** picks Clustal / Zappo / Taylor (proteins) or Nucleotide
   (DNA).
3. **`wrap_length=`, `show_consensus=`, `show_count=`** add the canonical
   Clustal-viewer scaffolding in three keyword arguments.
4. **`set_highlight_pos([(s,e)])`** boxes the regions the audience must look at.
5. **`.plotfig()` returns a matplotlib `Figure`** — cream-canvas rcParams and
   IBM Plex Mono apply for free.
:::

**Compare with:** the day-2 `_03_msa` build teaches the **primitives** — letter
grid, `imshow` colour grid, conservation bar, zoom — so you understand what
every pixel is. Reach for **pyMSAviz** when the alignment **is** the figure and
you want the production output without rebuilding the wheel.
